questions.question: What is a 'performative' in FIPA-ACL terminology?
options: A tool the agent can call
The intent class of a message such as inform, request, or propose
The content language used to encode message payloads
A version identifier on the agent communication layer
questions.explanation: A performative is the verb of an ACL message. It states what the sender is doing with the utterance: informing, requesting, proposing, accepting, refusing. The performative is separate from the content, which carries the payload.

questions.question: Why did FIPA-ACL fade from industry around 2010?
options: It was superseded by a competing IEEE standard with better security
Ontology overhead was too heavy, tooling was Java-only, and the web stack won with REST and JSON
The performative catalog was too small to express modern agent behaviors
FIPA required paid licensing that prevented open-source adoption
questions.explanation: Three forces killed FIPA: requiring a shared ontology made integration a multi-year standards process; SL (Semantic Language) formal semantics were ignored by practitioners; and JADE was Java-only while REST+JSON was polyglot. The web won.

questions.question: Which 2026 protocol corresponds most closely to the FIPA 'request' performative?
options: A2A Agent Card discovery
MCP tools/call
ACP TrajectoryMetadata
ANP DID verification
questions.explanation: MCP tools/call carries the same envelope as a FIPA request: who, whom, intent, payload, correlation id. Both express 'I ask you to execute this action.' Liu et al. 2025 (arXiv:2505.02279) maps MCP to FIPA request/query-ref explicitly.

questions.question: In the Contract Net Protocol, what does a 'cfp' (call for proposals) message accomplish?
options: It acknowledges receipt of a task and moves its state to working
It cancels an ongoing negotiation that has reached deadlock
It broadcasts a task description to potential bidders who may respond with proposals
It confirms that a proposal has been accepted and execution can begin
questions.explanation: Contract Net Protocol starts with the manager issuing a cfp to broadcast the task. Bidders respond with propose messages. The manager then sends accept-proposal to the winner and reject-proposal to the others. This is the canonical task-market pattern.

questions.question: What is 'semantic drift' and which FIPA mechanism was designed to prevent it?
options: Agents slowly changing their system prompts during long runs; prevented by role pinning
Two agents using the same word for different concepts without detection; prevented by requiring a shared ontology on message content
A reply-with correlation id becoming stale after timeouts; prevented by re-issuing conversation ids
Tool schemas becoming inconsistent across agent versions; prevented by pinning spec versions
questions.explanation: Semantic drift: two agents both use 'customer' but mean different things. FIPA's ontology field required both parties to declare a shared ontology; the message was rejected at parse time if the receiver did not recognize it. Modern JSON protocols drop the ontology and let LLMs infer meaning, reintroducing this failure mode.
